summary.headline: Craftsman guides consolidated net debt/EBITDA of 1.7-1.8x for FY27 as Aluminium margins dip on a one-time raw material impact, with a $100M stationary-engine revenue peak targeted for FY30.
summary.overview: Management described Q2 FY27 as a build-up quarter: large capacity has been added, some lines are not yet full, and gross profit is growing about 30% YoY in H1. Aluminium EBIT margin fell to about 6.5% in the quarter, which management attributed to inventory bought during raw material shortages being consumed as aluminium prices fell, plus ramp-up costs at new plants and gas cost inflation. Gross debt rose from Rs 3,340 crore (Mar 2026) to Rs 3,618 crore (Sep 2026) despite QIP proceeds, due to working capital, GST credits, and capex. Management is pursuing price resets with OEMs on legacy products and sees Sunbeam exiting low-margin customers.

financial_highlights.value: about 30% YoY in H1 and Q2 (as stated by analyst; management affirmed continued YoY growth for next 2-3 quarters)

financial_highlights.change: decline from normal run rate of about 12-13% (analyst's framing)

financial_highlights.value: about Rs 1,100 crore (analyst's figure, not disputed)

financial_highlights.metric: Share of revenue from German subsidiary

segments.name: Powertrain
segments.commentary: Management expects growth to continue across most sub-segments through the next two to three quarters, with tractor contracting over the next two quarters. Powertrain plants are described as mature and at good operating leverage.

segments.name: Aluminium
segments.commentary: Margins were hit by ramp-up costs at new plants, a one-time raw material impact from aggressive buying during shortages and falling prices, and gas cost inflation. Management expects marginal impact in Q3 and nothing in Q4, with price corrections to be negotiated with OEMs.

segments.name: Sunbeam
segments.commentary: Low-margin customers are being exited, with support continuing through the festive season. Management expects top line to fall but absolute margins to improve, and expects Q3 and Q4 to look better with new customers next year.

segments.name: Stationary engines (data centre)
segments.commentary: Order book of about $100 million, with revenue starting FY29 and peaking around $100 million in FY30. Management guided to 30% of order book by FY28 and 50% by FY29, reaching run rate by Q3 or Q4 of FY30.

guidance_outlook: Consolidated net debt/EBITDA of 1.7x-1.8x for FY27.
Internal critical inflection at around Rs 1,850 crore EBITDA, expected next year, after which capex and maintenance capex are self-funded.
Committed 15% CAGR in real terms (not inflation-adjusted), with some years higher.
Q3 FY27 consolidated capex of Rs 500-600 crore; Q4 capex expected to be low as long-term capex is pushed to later years.
Price resets sought of about 6-7% up to 15-20% on value-add (not top line), depending on commodity, product and order timing.
Aluminium margins expected to normalise after customer negotiations, with benefits in the next two quarters; management declined to quantify the margin.
capex_capacity: Stationary engine capex largely done; revenues from data-centre stationary engines to start FY29 and peak around $100 million in FY30.
Greenfield facilities put up across India in powertrain and aluminium; land acquired for 3-5 years of expansion with basic infrastructure in place, so further equipment needs less capex.
Aluminium new plants are running at suboptimal utilisation and need about two quarters to reach operating leverage; mature plants have better leverage.

German subsidiary: foundry is the only manufacturing entity; a small machine shop (about Rs 20-30 crore on a couple of machines) is planned to reduce working capital. Management said it is not a fan of large overseas investment.
Second phase of stationary-engine capacity is under inquiry and is expected to be less capital intensive given existing foundry and machine shop infrastructure.
demand_pricing: Management says inquiries for the next level of stationary-engine capacity remain strong, mostly on existing products.
Legacy product price resets are being sought across OEMs due to manpower, energy and consumables inflation; management says new products are being priced at new prices.
Management said it is more selective on customers and products, favouring larger customers and more profitable products.
Passenger vehicle aluminium content in India is about one-third of developed markets as a share of vehicle weight, which management sees as a long runway.
Management sees India as an export hub for powertrain aggregates from multinational OEMs, with 1.5 litre and below passenger vehicle engines cited.

qa_highlights.question: When will gross profit growth inflect, given capacity additions and new business wins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects YoY growth to continue for the next two to three quarters, supported by the pipeline and plants coming on stream; Aluminium new plants need about two more quarters to reach operating leverage.

qa_highlights.question: What price correction magnitude is needed to offset manpower, energy and other inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said corrections of 6-7% up to 15-20% are needed on value-add, varying by commodity, product and order timing, with no top-line impact expected.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross debt rise despite QIP proceeds, and what is the FY27 leverage?
qa_highlights.answer: Working capital, GST credits, safety stock and pipeline inventory rose along with capex; management guided to 1.7-1.8x consolidated net debt/EBITDA for the year and an EBITDA inflection at about Rs 1,850 crore next year.

qa_highlights.question: Has Sunbeam started exiting low-margin business and what is the margin path?
qa_highlights.answer: Smaller low-margin customers have largely exited; larger customers are being handheld until the festive season exit. Management expects top line to fall but absolute margins to improve, with some customers negative on EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Aluminium margin decline a mark-to-market loss, and how big is it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quantify, saying the impact is consumption cost rather than mark-to-market, with a one-time effect in Q2, marginal in Q3 and nil in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the stationary-engine order book converts to revenue by when?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 30% of the roughly $100 million order book by FY28 and 50% by FY29, with run rate reached by Q3 or Q4 of FY30.

risks_watch: Aluminium margin recovery depends on OEM price corrections and on how negotiations on past and future aluminium pass-through conclude; management could not quantify the amount.
Net debt and working capital: gross debt rose to Rs 3,618 crore; leverage target 1.7-1.8x depends on H2 EBITDA and working-capital release.
Tractor segment is expected to contract over the next two quarters.
Legacy product negotiations may lead to volume loss where capacity is not fungible, according to management.
Sunbeam top line will decline as low-margin customers exit; new customer wins are expected next year.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term growth and the FY30 peak, but cautious and somewhat evasive on quantification: management declined to quantify the aluminium impact, Q3 and Q4 margin trajectory, and EBITDA forecasts, and avoided sharing inquiry values.
key_quotes: So, the operating leverage on those plants will take another two quarters to get into a profitable situation, more profitable situation.
This is not on the top line, but on the gross margin or the value addition portion.
So, I would leave it at that.
So, overall I think we will be at 1.7-1.8 net debt to EBITDA on a consolidated basis for the year.

adds.what: Stationary engine second phase capacity under inquiry (not yet committed; less capital intensive)
Stationary engine data-centre revenue ramp: ~$100M order book, revenue starting FY29, peak FY30
Aluminium greenfield plants added (running at suboptimal utilisation, ~2 quarters to operating leverage)
German subsidiary small machine shop (Rs 20-30 crore, couple of machines)

growth.why: Management committed to a 15% real CAGR and guided FY27 consolidated net debt/EBITDA of 1.7-1.8x, backed by a ~$100M stationary-engine order book (30% by FY28, 50% by FY29), greenfield powertrain and aluminium plants, and OEM price resets of 6-7% to 15-20% on value-add; the quarter's gross profit growth (~30% YoY in H1) is an analyst figure, and capex is being pushed out in Q4.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Aluminium EBIT margin fell to about 6.5% vs a normal 12-13% run rate on a one-time raw material hit and ramp-up costs; management expects marginal impact in Q3, nil in Q4, and OEM price resets of 6-7% up to 15-20% on value-add, though it declined to quantify the recovery.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Aluminium greenfield plants are commissioned but at suboptimal utilisation and need about two quarters to reach operating leverage; stationary-engine capex is largely done, with data-centre revenue starting FY29 (about $100M order book, 30% by FY28, 50% by FY29).

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management committed to a 15% real CAGR and expects YoY gross profit growth to continue for 2-3 quarters, backed by a ~$100M stationary-engine order book; offset by Sunbeam top line falling as low-margin customers exit and tractor contracting over the next two quarters.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is only about 70% in recent months and H1 capex was about Rs 1,100 crore, with Q3 capex Rs 500-600 crore and Q4 capex cut as long-term capex is pushed into later years; a second stationary-engine phase is under inquiry and less capital intensive, so a fresh large capex is not expected near term.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management guided FY27 consolidated net debt/EBITDA of 1.7-1.8x and gross debt rose to Rs 3,618 crore from Rs 3,340 crore, with net debt around Rs 3,000 crore, so there is no sign of raising guidance; the ~30% H1 gross profit growth is an analyst figure, not a management guide.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Leverage target of 1.7-1.8x depends on H2 EBITDA and working-capital release, the Aluminium margin recovery is unquantified and tied to OEM negotiations, and legacy price resets may cost volume where capacity is not fungible.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Second phase of stationary-engine capacity is under inquiry and not yet committed, and inquiries for the next level of stationary-engine capacity are strong, mostly on existing products; no firm new-product date was given.

rows.label: OEM price resets on legacy products
rows.why: Management seeks about 6-7% up to 15-20% on value-add to offset manpower, energy and consumables inflation, with new products already priced at new prices; magnitude varies by commodity and order timing and is not yet secured.

rows.label: Internal critical inflection at Rs 1,850 crore EBITDA
rows.why: Management expects EBITDA to reach about Rs 1,850 crore next year, after which capex and maintenance capex become self-funded; net debt is around Rs 3,000 crore with gross debt of Rs 3,618 crore at Sep 2026.

rows.label: Working capital and GST credit release
rows.why: Gross debt rose from Rs 3,340 crore to Rs 3,618 crore on working capital, GST credits and safety stock, and leverage of 1.7-1.8x depends on working-capital release in H2.

tone.note: Management was confident on the 15% real CAGR, the FY30 stationary-engine peak and the 1.7-1.8x leverage target, but cautious and evasive on quantifying the Aluminium margin hit, Q3/Q4 margin path and EBITDA forecasts; analysts pressed on the size of the one-time Aluminium impact, the debt increase
